## Answer

**Is PostgreSQL 16 supported under upstream community policy as of 2026-10-07? Yes.**

The PostgreSQL Global Development Group's own Versioning Policy page (www.postgresql.org/support/versioning/, linked from the community Support section) lists version 16 as **Supported: Yes**, with first release September 14, 2023 and final release **November 9, 2028**. Since October 7, 2026 precedes that final-release date, major version 16 remains a supported release under upstream community policy — no vendor extended-support program involved.

**How long are major versions supported, and when does the clock start?**

The community policy states: *"The PostgreSQL Global Development Group supports a major version for 5 years after its initial release. After this, a final minor version will be released and the software will then be unsupported (end-of-life)."* So the support window is **5 years from the major version's initial (first .0) release**, not from any later point. The table's Final Release column confirms this pattern: 16's final release (Nov 9, 2028) is 5 years past its first release (Sept 14, 2023) plus a short extension so the last minor lands on the community's scheduled November release day. The same upstream page notes each major version gets minor releases (bug/security fixes) at least quarterly until then.

**Does installing a newer 16.x minor restart the clock? No.**

Nothing in the written policy ties the support clock to minor-version updates. The support duration is defined solely as "5 years after its initial release" of the *major version*, and the release table's rows — "First Release" and "Final Release" — are keyed by major version (16 as a whole, not per 16.x minor). Minor releases are described as containing only bug, security, and data-corruption fixes, with no lifecycle effect. The final 16.x minor (a future 16.x listed as the final release on November 9, 2028) will be the last one for the entire series, and at that point the whole major version becomes end-of-life regardless of which 16.x minor you installed or when. Upgrading to a newer 16.x minor only gets you current with fixes (the policy explicitly recommends always running the current minor release); it does not extend or reset the end-of-life date.

**Notes on sources and limitations:** The core facts come from the live, official Versioning Policy page fetched directly (primary community source), supplemented by a web search that corroborated the same table and the November 9, 2028 final-release date (e.g., Azure and RDS official docs mirror the community EOL date; endoflife.ai states point releases share the major version's EOL date). One minor discrepancy exists in the wider ecosystem: some tertiary sources cite PG 16's announcement date as September 11, 2023, while the community's own table uses September 14, 2023 as the first release; the official table is authoritative here. The community page does not include a separate FAQ explicitly addressing "minor upgrade restarts the clock," so that conclusion is based on the literal wording of the support-term definition (clock pegged to the major version's initial release) rather than an explicit negative statement — though the release-calendar structure (Final Release tied to the major version) makes any other reading untenable.
